packageRules.description: Node.js and npm come from the target OS, not from Renovate: the .deb runs on the nodejs and npm that apt installs, and the oldest supported OS is Raspberry Pi OS Bookworm / Debian 12 with Node.js 18.20.4 and npm 9.2.0. The constraints above make Renovate generate lock files with exactly that toolchain and skip every release whose engines exclude it. .nvmrc, backend/package.json engines and these constraints are changed together, by hand, when Bookworm support is dropped
Node.js type definitions have to describe the oldest supported Node.js (see above), not the newest

TypeScript 6 needs typescript-eslint >= 8.56, which requires Node.js 20 (see eslint-config-love below). TypeScript 7 is also a native compiler binary that is not published for linux-ia32, and the i386 .deb is compiled inside an i386 container

eslint-config-love declares no engines, so the constraints above cannot filter it: from 152 on it needs typescript-eslint >= 8.56 (eslint-visitor-keys 5), from 154 eslint-plugin-n 18 and from 156 ESLint 10, all of which require Node.js 20. The lock file keeps typescript-eslint at 8.55.0 for the same reason
package.json engines declare the supported Node.js range; keep them as ranges instead of pinning them to a single release
Safely automerge patch and digest updates
npm minor/patch updates - one PR per package so a single failure doesn't block the rest
